summary: OpenAI announced on Friday, Nov. 17, 2023, that it had pushed out co-founder and CEO Sam Altman after a board review found he was "not consistently candid in his communications." Chief technology officer Mira Murati became interim CEO, and board chairman Greg Brockman quit, saying he and Altman were shocked by the board's action. The article covers Altman's background, OpenAI's shift from nonprofit to a for-profit arm, Microsoft's reaction, analyst commentary, and Altman's other ventures.
one_line: OpenAI's board fired CEO Sam Altman for not being consistently candid, prompting Greg Brockman to quit and Mira Murati to become interim CEO.
key_facts: OpenAI said Friday it pushed out co-founder and CEO Sam Altman after a review found he was "not consistently candid in his communications" with the board.
Mira Murati, OpenAI's chief technology officer, became interim CEO effective immediately while the company searches for a permanent replacement.
Greg Brockman, board chairman and president, was removed as chairman; he then posted on X that he quit, writing "based on today's news, i quit."
Brockman said Altman was asked to join a noon Friday video meeting with board members (minus Brockman), where Chief Scientist Ilya Sutskever told Altman he was being fired.
OpenAI declined to say what Altman's alleged lack of candor was about, saying his behavior hindered the board's ability to exercise its responsibilities.
The board consists of Ilya Sutskever and three non-employees: Quora CEO Adam D'Angelo, Tasha McCauley, and Helen Toner of the Georgetown Center for Security and Emerging Technology.
Microsoft, which has invested billions in OpenAI, said the transition won't affect the relationship and that it remains committed to Mira and their team.
Altman, now 38, helped start OpenAI as a nonprofit research lab in 2015, and was recruited in 2014 to lead startup incubator YCombinator.
In 2018 OpenAI incorporated a for-profit business, Open AI LP, and Elon Musk resigned from the board to avoid a "potential future conflict for Elon" with Tesla's self-driving work.
The U.S. Federal Trade Commission has launched an investigation into whether OpenAI violated consumer protection laws by scraping public data and publishing false information.
Days before the firing, Altman headlined OpenAI's first developer conference and then paused new ChatGPT premium subscriptions because capacity was exceeded.
Forrester analyst Rowan Curran said the exit seemed to be about the individual, "not with the underlying technology or business."
Altman's other bets include Helion Energy (fusion), Retro Biosciences (aims to add 10 years to human lifespan), and Worldcoin (biometric crypto project).
